items.followUp: What is the purpose of the title element in the head section of an HTML document?

rubric.why: Identifies the head section's role in holding document information that is not shown as page content.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it contains document information or metadata that is not displayed in the webpage body.

rubric.why: Shows the HTML tags that enclose the head section.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly giving both opening and closing head tags.

modelAnswer: The head section contains information about an HTML document, such as its title, that is not displayed as the main content of the webpage.
It is written between the <head> and </head> tags.

items.followUp: Write HTML code to make the text “Open picture” a hyperlink to photo.jpg.

rubric.why: Checks that the answer uses an anchor element with an href destination for the image.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using an <a> element and giving the image file as its href destination.

rubric.why: Checks that the link has clickable content, either link text or an image.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including suitable clickable text or an image inside the anchor element.

modelAnswer: Write an anchor element and set its href attribute to the image file.
Place clickable text or an image between the opening and closing anchor tags, for example: View image.

items.followUp: Describe the steps you would take to plan an algorithm that calculates the average of three numbers.

rubric.why: Planning begins by understanding and clearly defining the problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the problem and its requirements must first be understood.

rubric.why: Identifying the required inputs and expected outputs clarifies what the solution must do.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the data needed and the result required.

rubric.why: A solution plan sets out a logical sequence of steps.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing how to devise logical steps or an algorithm.

rubric.why: A plan can be represented in a clear form before implementation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a suitable representation, such as a flowchart or pseudocode.

modelAnswer: Planning a solution means deciding in advance how a problem will be solved.
First, understand and clearly define the problem and its requirements.
Identify the input data, the processing needed, and the expected output.
Develop a logical sequence of steps (an algorithm) and represent it using pseudocode or a flowchart.

items.followUp: Name the four-layer TCP/IP model and briefly state the function of each layer.

rubric.why: The application layer provides network services to user applications.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming this layer and stating its role in providing network services to applications.

rubric.why: The transport layer manages end-to-end delivery of data between devices.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming this layer and describing end-to-end delivery or reliable data transfer.

rubric.why: The Internet layer handles logical addressing and routing packets between networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming this layer and stating its routing or IP addressing function.

rubric.why: The data link and physical layers handle local-link framing and the transmission of bits over the medium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both layers and describing their role in sending data over the physical network medium.

modelAnswer: The TCP/IP model is a layered framework that describes how data is communicated over networks.
Application layer: provides network services used by applications, such as web and email services.
Transport layer: provides end-to-end communication and manages the delivery of data between devices.
Internet layer: uses IP addressing and routing to move packets between networks.
Data link layer: organises data for transmission over a local network link.
Physical layer: transmits bits as signals over the physical communication medium.

items.followUp: What is an algorithm, and how does it help in solving a problem?

rubric.why: Problem solving is a planned, systematic process rather than a guess.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing problem solving as a systematic or step-by-step process.

rubric.why: The process is undertaken to find a solution to the problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the process aims to find or implement a solution.

modelAnswer: Problem solving is a systematic, step-by-step process of understanding a problem and finding a solution to it.

items.followUp: Which flowchart symbol is used for input and output, and what does it represent?

rubric.why: A rectangle is the standard flowchart symbol for a process.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the process symbol as a rectangle.

rubric.why: The process symbol represents an operation or instruction performed in the solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it represents processing, an operation, a calculation, or an instruction.

modelAnswer: The process symbol in a flowchart is a rectangle.
It represents a processing step, such as an instruction, operation, or calculation.

items.followUp: What is an anchor link, and how can it be used to jump to a section on the same webpage?

rubric.why: A hyperlink is a clickable connection to another page or resource.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for distinguishing a hyperlink as a clickable link to another page or resource.

rubric.why: An anchor identifies a location within a page that a link can jump to.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that an anchor links to a named or specific location, commonly within the same page.

modelAnswer: A hyperlink is a clickable link that takes the user to another webpage or resource.
An anchor identifies a specific location in a webpage, allowing a link to jump directly to that location, often on the same page.

items.followUp: Convert the binary number 1011₂ to decimal and explain the place values used.

rubric.why: Binary is a base-two number system.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the binary number system has base 2.

rubric.why: Binary uses only the digits 0 and 1, with positions representing powers of two.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it uses digits 0 and 1 and/or that its place values are powers of 2.

modelAnswer: The binary number system has base 2 and uses only the digits 0 and 1.
Each position in a binary number has a place value that is a power of 2.
